assumptions.assumption: The existing Object::IrTimer represents the extended kernel timer used by the observed NtSetTimer2 call.
assumptions.basis: Guest trace: handle0x2c, attributes8, timer_idNone, dormant signal; independent native exact request succeeds. Existing NtCreateTimer2 implementation records all extended types as IrTimer.; all four native constructor/set/cancel profiles, shared dispatcher/HLE state and real installed host/WoW64 leaves agree.
assumptions.dependent-result: Add real arming/cancellation state to this object rather than legacy Object::Timer.
assumptions.stress-test: Native regular/extended/event/invalid handles, all supported constructor attribute families and access grants.
assumptions.falsification-probe: Native NtSetTimer2 accepts a different dispatcher object or existing constructor representation disagrees with native type capture.

assumptions.assumption: Version/Reserved/NoWakeTolerance layout is two ULONGs plus LONGLONG in16bytes.
assumptions.basis: Stored pinned PHNT ntexapi.h lines1373-1394 and exact native ctypes sizeof16 success.; native value/fault matrix confirms full16-byte read, ignored Reserved, validation and ABI-specific capture order.
assumptions.dependent-result: Input capture, cross-ABI parsing and time-unit model.
assumptions.stress-test: All pointer alignments, crossing/guard/noaccess pages, nonzero version/reserved, boundary tolerance values; WoW64 fault ordering.
assumptions.falsification-probe: Native captures use different offsets/size or branch semantics than the declaration.

assumptions.assumption: All native test operations remain confined to anonymous handles in their own producer processes.
assumptions.basis: Fixed creation API, no object names, no host policy writes and unconditional cancellation/close cleanup.; producer handle counts balance and PE/source/runtime identities remain unchanged.
assumptions.stress-test: Check handle counts, guard regions, before/after module and producer hashes; avoid unbounded waits.
assumptions.falsification-probe: Handle leak, non-private target, global policy mutation or an unbounded wait.

assumptions.assumption: Relative Timer2 uses the suspend-excluding clock domain documented for modern Windows waitable timers.
assumptions.basis: Stored Microsoft SetWaitableTimerEx Windows8+ clock contract, extended dispatcher model, and the existing three-platform native deadline adapter.
assumptions.dependent-result: Relative Timer2 deadlines and periodic scheduling reuse the native awake-time adapter; UTC absolute targets remain independent.
assumptions.stress-test: Full signed interval boundaries, synthetic UTC adjustments, periodic phase/skip arithmetic, native clock adapters on all hosts.
assumptions.falsification-probe: A controlled native NtSetTimer2 suspend/resume experiment in an isolated machine counts host low-power time against a relative target.
assumptions.status: retained: physical NtSetTimer2 suspend/resume experiment is unknown and is not claimed
